confirmed: Read the complete 188-line markdown and all 9 PDF pages, including limitations, references, author biography, and license; there are no appended studies or appendices in this PDF. PDF pp. 1-9.

The source is the published DRS conference paper by Katelijn Quartier, DOI 10.21606/drsf.119, for the 2025 colloquium in Milan, 14-15 May. The PDF has a DRS cover sheet plus printed pp. 151-158 and a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 license. PDF pp. 1-2 and 9. The form's version-of-record description is supported.

There is one original study comparing consecutive academic-year cohorts: 2022-2023 without AI, 2023-2024 taught Midjourney during store development, and 2024-2025 taught it during concept development. These are existing yearly classes, not randomized groups. quasi_people and context_class=observational are supported; no randomized people study appears anywhere in the paper. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 153), Section 2.

The printed group counts are 6, 11, and 6 students, not designs, ideas, ratings, or randomized allocations. They imply fewer than 50 people even before any unreported exclusions. The limitations repeat 6-11 students per year; 23 is not printed as a total analyzed count. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 153), Section 2; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 157), Section 6.

Midjourney is a text-to-image tool used to generate concept boards and visual inspiration; its version is not stated for this study. Training was a half-day session followed by two hands-on exercises. Students designed a luxury-brand concept store within a 400 m2 space. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 153), Section 2; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 155), Section 4.1.

Two teachers, a retail design expert and the author, guided the work. Designs and process documentation were evaluated on innovativeness, originality, and creativity; the latter concerns depth and meaningfulness of ideas. These are qualitative assessments of produced work, not solely self-reported creativity. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 154), Section 3.

S1-O1 reported quotation matches: "there was a noticeable increase in the creativity factor, particularly in Group 3." The surrounding text describes stronger conceptual storytelling and more cohesive concepts; it gives no numerical creativity score or effect estimate. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 156), first Section 4.2.

S1-O2 reported quotation matches: "An analysis of the students' results revealed no significant impact on two of the three predetermined evaluation criteria: innovativeness and originality." No test statistic or p-value accompanies significant. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 156), first Section 4.2.

S1-O3 reported quotation matches: "the extent to which the designs introduced new solutions, and their uniqueness compared to existing designs remained relatively consistent across all groups." This supports no_clear_difference as a qualitative direction, rather than a numerical null estimate. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 156), first Section 4.2.

Process timing is reported as seven weeks of initial research and analysis followed by another seven weeks of design for Group 1; Group 2 followed the same timeline. Group 3 reduced the need for an additional one to two weeks of manual concept-board creation. The abstract also says early-stage development was reduced by 1-2 weeks. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 156), second Section 4.2; PDF p. 2 (printed p. 151), Abstract.

There are no tables, numerical creativity ratings, effect sizes, intervals, or significance tests to extract. The author says a quantitative component or statistical analysis would strengthen the findings. PDF pp. 5-9, especially p. 9 (printed p. 158), concluding limitations paragraph; table detection found no tables on any PDF page.

This is not a synthesis, so synthesis fields appropriately contain no study counts or pooled estimates. No across-person diversity score or post-AI test is reported. Core exclusion is supported by nonrandom allocation and cohort sizes below 50. PDF pp. 4-9, Sections 2-6.
summary: This published conference paper compares three nonrandomized student cohorts of 6, 11, and 6 and belongs in observational context, with no randomized people study. The three quoted findings match the PDF, but the analyzed total, outcome units, unsupported metadata, task duration, and wording of the one-line finding need correction.
